h: Suffolk food, steam and a day in Stowmarket
p: The Food Museum is a brilliant fit for a day exploring mid Suffolk. Its focus on how food gets from field to plate means there's always something new to learn, whether it's how flour was milled, how cattle were reared or how kitchens have changed over the years. The estate stretches out across meadows, riverside paths and woodland, making it a peaceful place to wander, even when there aren't events on.

Keep an eye out for the steam engines and farm machinery that are fired up on special days. These hulking giants of the farming world are a sight to behold when they're working, and they help explain the huge changes to agriculture over the past century and a bit. The crafts, workshops and gardens add more layers, and there's often a seasonal theme running through activities.

Stowmarket town centre is right on the doorstep, so lunch in town is easy, or you could bring a picnic and settle down on the grass. Needham Lake, a few miles south at Needham Market, is a lovely spot for a walk or a play in the park beside the water.

Further afield, the Mid-Suffolk Light Railway at Wetheringsett recreates a little rural branch line, with steam trains on certain days, and Bury St Edmunds is a short drive west with its abbey gardens, cathedral and handsome Georgian streets. Put a couple of these together and you've got a great Suffolk weekend, with history and food at the heart of it all.
